editorial.headline: Nationally Open, but Bali Blocks Sharia Capital-Market Advice
editorial.standfirst: This sharia advisory activity permits full foreign ownership nationally, yet PMA registration at a Bali address is blocked by the province’s permanent moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity through a PMA company at a Bali address today, even though it is nationally open. This activity concerns sharia advisory work for the capital market: advising on, and/or overseeing, the application of sharia principles in a company’s business activities; and/or issuing a statement that a sharia capital-market product or service conforms with those principles. It is work rooted in applied sharia knowledge and experience, directed at how those principles are put into practice and evidenced in the capital-market setting.

The activity may be undertaken by an individual who has sharia knowledge and experience, or by a business entity whose management and employees have that knowledge and experience. The record makes the activity available at micro, small, medium and large scales, so the form of registration can follow the scale of the enterprise. Its scope is deliberately specific: the advisory and oversight functions sit alongside the ability to give a sharia-conformity statement for products or services in the capital market. That makes the underlying expertise—not a generic corporate label—the centre of the activity described.

Nationally, the position is clear. The activity is open to PMA and permits a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For an investor reviewing the national framework alone, that is a fully foreign-owned route rather than a capped foreign stake. Bali requires a separate conclusion. The record classifies the large-scale route as Medium-Low risk, bringing it within Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The result is not a reduced Bali ownership percentage; it is a block on PMA registration for a Bali address. The provincial position is linked to a Governor’s letter issued in May 2026. National openness therefore remains real, but it does not create an available PMA registration path in Bali for this activity.
